history.summary: CSV town 'Kurnool' is the district - actual town is Mantralayam (formerly Manchale). Sri Raghavendra Tirtha, the 17th-century Dvaita Vedanta saint and pontiff, entered jeeva samadhi (living tomb) here on the banks of the Tungabhadra in 1671 AD; devotees believe he dwells in the Brindavana alive for 700 years blessing pilgrims. The Brindavana is the sanctum of the Sri Raghavendra Swamy Mutt (srsmatha.org); three chariots (gold, silver, wooden) carry the saint's idol in daily procession. The Manchalamma temple (village deity) is traditionally visited before entering the Mutt.

name: Sri Raghavendra Swamy Brindavanam, Mantralayam
town_description: Mantralayam (earlier Manchale) is a temple town in Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh, on the banks of the Tungabhadra river near the Karnataka border. It is one of South India's premier Vaishnavite pilgrimage centres, built around the Brindavana of Sri Guru Raghavendra Swamy, with the Panchamukhi Anjaneya temple and Alampur's Navabrahma temples among nearby attractions.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~210-250 km)
travel.railway: Mantralayam Road station (MALM, ~8-16 km); Raichur Junction (~34 km)
travel.road: Well connected by APSRTC and private buses; ~250 km from Hyderabad, ~350 km from Bengaluru by road

visitor_information.best_time: Throughout the year; October-March is most pleasant, and the annual Aradhana in Shravana (Aug-Sep) is the grandest time
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning darshan 6:00 AM-2:00 PM; evening darshan 4:00 PM-9:00 PM (official srsmatha.org timings; temple closed 2:00-4:00 PM)
